label: context.reference
text:
A run is a JSON record naming its EE, worker pin, active checkpoints and interface-owned state. Its input and result travel through declared interface bindings. Use an available composition operation when it expresses the work; otherwise author the relevant records through permitted file tools. The bound task-authoring guide contains the run schema and guidance for connecting owners.

Choose boundaries that fit the task. Reuse existing work and interfaces where their state and authority fit. Use independent interface identities where conversations, execution state or permissions must remain separate. A new EE is useful when the goal or policy boundary warrants one, not merely because another run is needed. The new run's authority comes from its own worker ceiling and EE chain.

Find both ends of each connection. The recipient needs an active input route and enough readable context to act; the producer needs the corresponding output route. Tool requests and results have their own paths. Check the installed owner's contract for state and future templates coupled to a route before editing it. Preserve pending work and give a changed one-shot obligation a fresh generation.

Use artifact.send when choosing an addressed destination supported by the current grant and tool contract. Its admission result confirms the emission; completion and replies need their own evidence. When work should wait, leave a receiving binding. Add a verifier only when later work needs the specific proof it provides.
description: Choose run boundaries and connect producers, consumers and useful waits under their actual authority.
